title: Explore the customer table
prompt: List customer names and countries, ordered alphabetically by customer name.
answer: SELECT customername, country FROM customers ORDER BY customername;
hint: Choose customername and country from customers, then ORDER BY customername.

title: Countries represented
prompt: Return each distinct country represented in customers, sorted alphabetically.
answer: SELECT DISTINCT country FROM customers ORDER BY country;
hint: DISTINCT removes repeated rows in the output.

title: Orders in 2024
prompt: List ordernumber and orderdate for orders placed during calendar year 2024, oldest first.
answer: SELECT ordernumber, orderdate FROM orders WHERE orderdate >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND orderdate < DATE '2025-01-01' ORDER BY orderdate;
hint: Use two date boundaries; the end boundary is exclusive.

title: Orders with customer names
prompt: List every ordernumber and its customername, sorted by ordernumber.
starter: SELECT \nFROM orders o\nJOIN customers c USING (customernumber)
answer: SELECT o.ordernumber, c.customername FROM orders o JOIN customers c USING (customernumber) ORDER BY o.ordernumber;
hint: An order joins to exactly one customer using customernumber.

title: Products that never sold
prompt: List productcode and productname for products with no order details, sorted by productname.
answer: SELECT p.productcode, p.productname FROM products p LEFT JOIN orderdetails od USING(productcode) WHERE od.ordernumber IS NULL ORDER BY p.productname;
hint: A LEFT JOIN preserves products that have no matching orderdetails; select the missing side with IS NULL.

title: Customers per country
prompt: List country and number of customers as customer_count, sorted by country.
starter: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customer_count\nFROM customers
answer: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY country ORDER BY country;
hint: Each country needs its own group.

title: Count all customers' orders
prompt: List customernumber and count of orders as order_count for EVERY customer (including those with zero orders), sorted by customernumber.
answer: SELECT c.customernumber, COUNT(o.ordernumber) AS order_count FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o USING(customernumber) GROUP BY c.customernumber ORDER BY c.customernumber;
hint: Start at customers, LEFT JOIN orders, and COUNT(o.ordernumber) instead of COUNT(*).

title: Avoid multiplying payment totals
prompt: Homework 8, Query 3: list customernumber, customername, and SUM of payments as total_payments for customers with payments. List each once, sorted by customername. Do not join orders: it multiplies payments and drops customers with no orders.
starter:
SELECT c.customernumber, c.customername, SUM(p.amount) AS total_payments
FROM customers c
JOIN payments p USING (customernumber)
JOIN orders o USING (customernumber)
GROUP BY c.customernumber, c.customername
ORDER BY c.customername;
answer: SELECT c.customernumber, c.customername, SUM(p.amount) AS total_payments FROM customers c JOIN payments p USING(customernumber) GROUP BY c.customernumber,c.customername ORDER BY c.customername;
hint: An unnecessary join to orders multiplies payment rows. SUM(DISTINCT amount) is not safe when two payments have equal amounts.

title: Orders with subtotal above 1,000
prompt: List ordernumber and SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) as subtotal for orders whose subtotal exceeds 1000. Sort by ordernumber.
starter: SELECT ordernumber, SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) AS subtotal\nFROM orderdetails
answer: SELECT ordernumber, SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) AS subtotal FROM orderdetails GROUP BY ordernumber HAVING SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) > 1000 ORDER BY ordernumber;
hint: The condition is on an aggregate, so it belongs in HAVING.

title: Exclude every oversized purchase
prompt: Homework 8, Query 5: list productcode and productname of products that NEVER appear in an order detail with quantityordered > 48. Include products never ordered. Sort by productname.
starter:
SELECT DISTINCT p.productcode, p.productname
FROM products p
INNER JOIN orderdetails od USING(productcode)
WHERE od.quantityordered <= 48
ORDER BY p.productname;
answer: SELECT p.productcode, p.productname FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orderdetails od WHERE od.productcode = p.productcode AND od.quantityordered > 48) ORDER BY p.productname;
hint: Find bad productcodes (quantity > 48), then exclude them. Never-ordered products must remain.

title: All orders tied for biggest subtotal
prompt: Homework 8, Query 4: list ordernumber and subtotal for every order tied at the maximum subtotal, sorted by ordernumber. The subtotal is SUM(quantityordered * priceeach).
starter: SELECT ordernumber, SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) AS subtotal\nFROM orderdetails\nGROUP BY ordernumber
answer: WITH totals AS (SELECT ordernumber, SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) AS subtotal FROM orderdetails GROUP BY ordernumber) SELECT ordernumber, subtotal FROM totals WHERE subtotal = (SELECT MAX(subtotal) FROM totals) ORDER BY ordernumber;
hint: Aggregate orderdetails first in a CTE. Compare each subtotal to MAX(subtotal) of that CTE.

title: One order, not one line item
prompt: Homework 8, Query 2: list each ordernumber ONCE if it has at least one orderdetail with quantityordered > 50. Sort by ordernumber. Fix the provided query.
starter:
SELECT o.ordernumber
FROM orders o
JOIN orderdetails od USING(ordernumber)
WHERE od.quantityordered > 50
ORDER BY o.ordernumber;
answer: SELECT DISTINCT o.ordernumber FROM orders o JOIN orderdetails od USING(ordernumber) WHERE od.quantityordered > 50 ORDER BY o.ordernumber;
hint: A joined row is an order line, not an entire order. More than one line can satisfy the filter.

title: Payment duplication trap
prompt: Repair the query so that customers with payments appear once with the correct sum, even if they have multiple orders or no orders.
starter:
SELECT c.customernumber, c.customername, SUM(p.amount) AS total_payments
FROM customers c
JOIN payments p USING(customernumber)
JOIN orders o USING(customernumber)
GROUP BY c.customernumber,c.customername
ORDER BY c.customername;
answer: SELECT c.customernumber, c.customername, SUM(p.amount) AS total_payments FROM customers c JOIN payments p USING(customernumber) GROUP BY c.customernumber,c.customername ORDER BY c.customername;
hint: The orders join contributes nothing to the requested total and multiplies payment rows.

title: Keep every tied maximum
prompt: Fix Homework 8 Query 4. Return ordernumber and subtotal for every greatest-subtotal order, ordered by ordernumber. Avoid a tie-breaker that makes tied values appear different.
starter:
SELECT ordernumber, SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) AS subtotal
FROM orderdetails
GROUP BY ordernumber
ORDER BY subtotal DESC, ordernumber
FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY;
answer: WITH totals AS (SELECT ordernumber, SUM(quantityordered * priceeach) AS subtotal FROM orderdetails GROUP BY ordernumber) SELECT ordernumber, subtotal FROM totals WHERE subtotal=(SELECT MAX(subtotal) FROM totals) ORDER BY ordernumber;
hint: Ties apply to every ORDER BY expression; a unique ordernumber breaks ties. Compare to MAX(subtotal) instead.

title: Exclude the most common customer country
prompt: Homework 8, Query 1: count orders by year as order_year and num_orders, excluding countries with the most CUSTOMERS (including those with zero orders and all ties). Sort by year.
starter:
SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.orderdate) AS order_year, COUNT(*) AS num_orders
FROM orders o JOIN customers c USING(customernumber)
WHERE c.country NOT IN (
 SELECT country FROM customers JOIN orders USING(customernumber)
 GROUP BY country ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS WITH TIES
)
GROUP BY order_year ORDER BY order_year;
answer: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.orderdate) AS order_year, COUNT(*) AS num_orders FROM orders o JOIN customers c USING(customernumber) WHERE c.country NOT IN (SELECT country FROM customers GROUP BY country ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS WITH TIES) GROUP BY order_year ORDER BY order_year;
hint: The innermost query must count customers in customers, not joined orders. JOIN orders changes who is counted.
